adjudication_notes: Article reports separate landslides at Kharkhare Bhir and Puma Bhir, both blocking roads in Lamjung.
Evidence combines separate Kerabari road-blocking slides on Aug 31 and Sep 1; the Sep 1 event is real, but the cluster is not one physical event.
One article reports two distinct Sindhuli road-blocking failures, at Sunkoshi-2 and Golanjor-6; therefore the record is not one physical event.
Article is about an ADB climate-risk programme and mentions landslides only as a general hazard; no specific landslide event is reported.
Article aggregates many distinct landslides and other failures across several Chitwan highway locations.
The July 9 obstruction occurred at Besishahar Municipality-1 in Lamjung, not Tanahu. The cluster also includes a July 10 report describing another slide at the same road location.
The cluster mixes the June 22 Kalikhola obstruction with distinct June 27 landslides; the June 22 event exists but the merge spans separate failures.
Opinion/analysis article about tourism, disasters and COVID-19; it does not report a specific landslide event in Bara.
Article summarizes a scientific study of landslide patterns and past hazards; it is not a report of one specific landslide event.
The cluster combines Aug 7 Nagdi Khola and Aug 14 Mauwakhola/Chumlingtar/Kurintar failures; the Aug 14 obstruction is real but the merge spans separate events.
Article reports separate landslides at Asmod and Gaganekhola in Shubha Kalika-1, Kalikot; Surkhet is only part of the highway name.
The articles describe multiple landslides across Hupsekot, Baudikali and Bulingtar over about five days; the disruption began before July 1 and is not one physical event.
Evidence reports several distinct landslides within Phidim (and additional events elsewhere). Five Panchthar deaths were later reported, but they came from multiple physical failures.
Article reports the 2023 Jajarkot earthquake and earthquake deaths; landslides are mentioned only generally as secondary effects, not as the claimed specific fatal event.
Feature article published in 2023 recounts a 2015 Sankhuwasabha landslide as background for a film; it is not a landslide event on the claimed 2023 date.
The reported road closure was caused by heavy snowfall, not a landslide; a Kalikot landslide is mentioned only as a previously cleared obstruction.
Article reports landslides at two to three points near Siddhababa on the Butwal–Palpa road; the failure area is on the Palpa side, not simply Rupandehi.
COP-29 travel article only mentions past floods and landslides as examples of climate damage; it does not report a specific landslide on the claimed date.
The article describes two separate Bhimphedi landslides (wards 1 and 8), both reported as having occurred the previous night/day before the Aug 23 reopening.
Evidence describes several distinct Parbat landslides that night across Kusma and Modi; the later detailed report gives 11 deaths in Parbat, so the cluster is not a single event.

Five deaths occurred across at least two separate landslides in Khaniyabash on Wednesday night, June 27; the cluster includes additional distinct failures, so June 28 is not the event date and the merge is not one event.
Police reported landslides at three to four separate spots around Satatale, so the record does not represent one single physical failure.
The headline uses 'landslide' metaphorically for an internal political defection in the NCP; no physical landslide occurred.
Article is about restoring Melamchi water supply and only refers to earlier flood/landslide damage; it does not report a new landslide on the claimed date.

Article describes broad Friday flood-and-landslide disruption along BP Highway around Bhakundebesi/Mangaltar in Kavre, not one specific Kathmandu landslide; the exact hazard for a single failure is not identifiable.
The cluster merges a month-old hydro-canal landslide with a distinct road-blocking slide in Palpa; the road slide occurred the night before Aug 4, not on Aug 4.
Article discusses ongoing landslide risk and past damage in Solaghar without identifying a specific dated landslide event on 2015-09-13.
Article concerns relief/identity cards for landslide victims in Taplejung and does not describe a specific landslide event on the claimed date.
Article is a Syangja monsoon-risk/impact overview; Parbat appears only as a victim's home district, not as the location of a specific claimed landslide event.
The article describes a landslide damaging a truck in the Rasuwa customs yard and also separate landslides blocking the road; the specific title event is not itself a road-obstruction event.
Article is a national disaster-relief funding overview and does not identify a specific Kathmandu landslide/debris-flow event on the claimed date.

Article reports five landslide deaths across several distinct incidents in Bhojpur, including Tyamkemaiyung-9 and Ramprasad Rai RM; it is not one physical event, and the claimed municipality does not cover all incidents. Exact event dates are not stated.

Two landslides at Nagmandir and near Siddhababa Temple in Tinau-3 blocked the Butwal-Tansen road on Monday morning 2020-07-27; the record combines more than one failure and the claimed 2020-07-26 date is wrong.
The cluster contains separate Khahare slides on July 28 (morning and afternoon) plus another slide on Aug 4, so it merges multiple physical events.

The cluster merges many separate Ichchhyakamana road slides across June 9-26. A June 18 report says one Ghoptebhir/Thadokhola slide occurred at 11 p.m. the previous night (June 17), so the claimed date is supported but the merge is not.

Only article titles/metadata are present. They indicate real landslide impacts and 35 deaths, but do not establish one physical event, the Kathmandu location, exact event date, or whether both articles cover the same failure.
The January 2021 reconstruction article summarizes multiple Myagdi landslides from the previous monsoon, including Dhaulagiri and Malika; it does not support a new July 10, 2021 single event.

Several landslides at Ranchuli, Molpha and Furke blocked the Karnali Highway overnight on 2024-08-09. They were in Kalikot; Jumla is the road division/source location, and the record combines multiple failures.
The reported landslide was an underwater volcanic landslide associated with the 2018 Sunda Strait tsunami in Indonesia, not a Nepal/Lalitpur event.
The cluster includes a June 27 obstruction/car burial and a separate June 22 Kalikhola slide, so it spans multiple physical events despite a valid June 27 event.
The June 27 Chitwan obstruction is real and one article explicitly reports no casualty, but the cluster also includes a distinct June 22 slide.
The Simkot-Kharpu road was broken by landslides at 12-15 locations. The article does not give a single event date or clearly place every failure inside Kharpunath municipality.
One article reports the fatal Sirise/Numa landslide while the other describes separate landslides trapping Kanduwa village; both are in Sankhuwasabha but they are not one physical event.
The pack mixes a July 31 Kharkhare slide with separate July 28 obstructions in Besishahar; the claimed July 31 event is real but the cluster is not one event.
The article reports separate slides at Bhattedanda in Lalitpur and Sisneri in Makwanpur on the same morning, so the record is an aggregate rather than one physical event.
This is a nationwide roundup of 28 obstructed roads, not one physical failure. It lists a Surkhet-Dullu road but does not identify the exact failure point or event date.
The July 19 Naugad-6 landslide killed two, but the cluster also includes separate later landslides in Malikarjun and a dry-slide incident near Mahakali, so the merge is incorrect.

Monsoon-triggered landslides around Bamka Bazaar, Bajura began Sunday night 2017-07-09 and displaced multiple businesses. The article describes plural/ongoing failures rather than one specific physical slide.

The article is primarily about flood damage that destroyed the Mauwa Khola bridge. It only mentions vaguely that landslides put Trishuli-side houses at risk and does not identify a specific Chitwan landslide event.
This is an editorial about farmers and recurring national problems; flood and landslide are mentioned only generically, with no specific Chitwan debris-flow event.

The Tinau RM-5 Hiyunde Khola road was affected from 2022-09-01, but the article reports an earlier closure plus two new landslides overnight that also swept the diversion. It therefore combines more than one physical failure.
The hospital was damaged by rain-driven mud/debris movement and landslips, but the article describes an ongoing hazard rather than a clearly dated single failure.

The article describes continuing daily landslides at Kerauja plus separate failures in Uhiya and other northern Gorkha villages. A damaging slide occurred on the Wednesday immediately before the 2016-06-30 report (June 29), not on the claimed 2016-06-22 date.
This is an analytical/historical overview citing annual Sindhupalchok disaster totals, not evidence of one specific Aug 20 event with 44 deaths.

This is a national two-month monsoon-disaster summary covering many districts, hazards and events. The 231 deaths are the nationwide total from floods, landslides and lightning, not a single Kathmandu debris-flow event.
